```{python}
def generic_voltage_plot(series, legend_name, start_time, end_time, title_text, ymin=None, ymax=None, events=None, x_tick_interval=900000, lemur_x = 0.02, lemur_y = 0.02):
    
    df_to_plot = series.loc[start_time:end_time]
    
    fig = go.Figure()

    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=df_to_plot.index,
        y=df_to_plot,
        mode='lines',
        name=legend_name,
        line=dict(color='black', width=1.2)
        ))

    if events is not None:
        for event in events:
            fig.add_vline(x=event, line=dict(dash='dash', color='gray', width=2))

    # Mark +/- 200mV and +/- 800mV
    if ymin is None:
        try:
            ymin = round(df_to_plot.min().min() * 1000 - 1) / 1000
        except:
            ymin = 25000
    if ymax is None:
        try:
            ymax = round(df_to_plot.max().max() * 1000 + 1) / 1000
        except:
            ymax = 29000
    # fig.add_hrect(y0=ymin, y1=25000.2, fillcolor="gray", opacity=0.1, line_width=0)
    # fig.add_hrect(y0=ymin, y1=25000.8, fillcolor="gray", opacity=0.1, line_width=0)
    # fig.add_hrect(y0=25001.2, y1=ymax, fillcolor="gray", opacity=0.1, line_width=0)
    # fig.add_hrect(y0=25001.8, y1=ymax, fillcolor="gray", opacity=0.1, line_width=0)

    # thick black line at 27kV
    fig.add_hline(y=27000, line=dict(dash='dash', color='gray', width=2))

    # # Note FCR saturation at +/- 200mhz
    # fig.add_annotation(
    #     x=df_to_plot.index[0] + pd.Timedelta(seconds=0.2),
    #     y=25000,
    #     text="<i>FCR Saturation</i>",
    #     showarrow=False,
    #     font=dict(size=12)
    # )
    # Update layout
    fig.update_layout(
        title=title_text,
        title_font=dict(size=24),
        xaxis_title=None,
        yaxis_title='Voltage [V]',
        yaxis_title_font=dict(size=20),
        yaxis_range=[ymin, ymax],
        showlegend=True,
        legend=dict(
            font=dict(size=24),
            orientation='h',
            yanchor='bottom',
            y=0.905,
            xanchor='right',
            x=0.15
        ),
        xaxis=dict(
            tickfont=dict(size=20),
            showgrid=True,
            gridwidth=1,
            gridcolor='lightgray',
            dtick=x_tick_interval, # 15 minutes in milliseconds
            # Add x-axis line
            showline=True,
            linewidth=1,
            linecolor='gray',
        ),
        yaxis=dict(
            tickfont=dict(size=20),
            showgrid=True,
            gridwidth=1,
            gridcolor='lightgray',
            # Format ticks to show kV
            tickvals = list(range(int(round(ymin, -3)), int(round(ymax, -3))+1000, 1000)),
            ticktext=[f"{v/1000}kV" for v in list(range(int(round(ymin, -3)), int(round(ymax, -3))+1000, 1000))],
            range=[ymin, ymax],
            # Remove tickformat and ticksuffix since we're using custom labels
            # Add y-axis line
            showline=True,
            linewidth=1,
            linecolor='gray',
        ),
        height = 800,
        width = 2000,
        plot_bgcolor='white',
        paper_bgcolor='white',
        margin=dict(l=50, r=50, t=90, b=60)
    )
    
    # # Add Lemur logo
    # fig.add_layout_image(
    #     dict(
    #         source=Image.open(figures_dir / "lemur_logo_yellow.png"),
    #         xref="paper",
    #         yref="y",
    #         x=lemur_x,
    #         y=lemur_y,
    #         sizex=0.2,
    #         sizey=0.2,
    #         xanchor="left",
    #         yanchor="bottom"
    #     )
    # )
    
    fig.add_annotation(
        text="analysis: lemur, uniovi | data: shared privately",
        xref="paper",
        yref="paper",
        x=-0.01,
        y=1.05,
        xanchor="left",
        yanchor="top",
        showarrow=False,
        font=dict(
            size=12,
            color="gray"
        ),
        bgcolor="white"
    )
    
    return fig



# # Plot Toledo L1 Frequency
t_toledo_voltage_start = pd.to_datetime('2025-04-28 11:00:00').tz_localize('Europe/Madrid')
t_toledo_voltage_end = pd.to_datetime('2025-04-28 12:50:00').tz_localize('Europe/Madrid')
fig = generic_voltage_plot(toledo_data['AnalyzerL1PhaseVoltage'], 
    'Toledo L1 Voltage', 
    t_toledo_voltage_start, 
    t_toledo_voltage_end, 
    'Toledo L1 Voltage', 
    ymin=25800, 
    ymax=29200, 
    x_tick_interval=900000, lemur_x = 0.015, lemur_y = 25800)
fig.show()
fig.write_image(figures_dir / f"toledo_l1_voltage_plot.png")
```
